newsitem.title: FRANCE: France seeks close but updated ties with Africa.
newsitem.headline: France seeks close but updated ties with Africa.

text.p: Prime Minister Lionel Jospin said on Thursday that he favoured continued close ties with France's former colonies in Africa but the relationship neeed to be adapted to modern times.

"The government is made up of men and women who were brought up in the culture of friendship with Africa...but our policies must be adapted to the problems of the times," Jospin said after talks with Chadian President Idriss Deby.
Deby, on the second day of a five-day state visit to France, met Jospin, a Socialist whose leftist government took power just one month ago, after lunching with conservative President Jacques Chirac.

Junior Minister for Cooperation Charles Josselin earlier testified before a National Assembly committee that Franco-African cooperation required "a renewed dialogue, an adult dialogue with Africans capable of assuming their own responsibilities, particularly with respect to security."
France has been drawn into a variety internal conflicts in its Africa in recent years, including a humanitarian mission in Rwanda and a series of attempted mutinies in the Central African Republic.

It also pushed the international community to send a humanitarian force into the former Zaire to prop up its ailing leader Mobutu Sese Seko before the central African nation fell to the rebel forces of Laurent kabila.
But it has now shown increasing reticence to become involved in internal conflicts on the continent and Jospin pledged on taking office last month to reevaluate relations with Africa.

During fighting in the Congo capital Brazzaville, France sent in troops only to evacuate foreign nationals and quickly withdrew them despite pleas by President Pascal Lissouba to remain as a buffer force between his soldiers and forces loyal to former president Denis Sassou Nguesso.
Deby said after his talks with Chirac and Jospin that relations with Paris were "perfectly fine". "It is a very healthy relationship, which is continuing to develop," he said.
He said the talks centred on the current situation in Chad, which he said was stable and making progress towards democracy after a long war.

Deby, a former guerrilla leader from the Moslem north, seized power in a 1990 French-backed coup after decades of civil war and conflict with Libya. After repeated electoral delays, he won a multi-party presidential poll in July.
